messages:
rachel: Observing an odd packing gap in prod-ap-northeast1. Many tiny inference pods Pending while a new 'bridge-pool' shows ~0.5 GPU free on several nodes. Started ~35m ago.
yusuf: Grafana: cluster/gpu_pending_count=72, bridge-pool/avg_free=0.48, warmpool/util=20%.
pete: we rolled the new bridge-pool last night to host fractional workloads between dedicated and shared racks. Could be the allocator not honoring the pool label.
lina: paste of `kubectl get pods -n prod | grep Pending` (trimmed):
```
mini-service-02     Pending   0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) didn't match node selector
rerank-lite-11      Pending   0/1 nodes are available: 1 node(s) had taints that the pod didn't tolerate
```
rachel: autoscaler logs show scale attempts but cloud returned `InsufficientCapacity` for the region at 1854322035 — quota seems ok but specific instance types for bridge-pool failing. cloud-ops-bot, any insights?
cloud-ops-bot: Observed spot supply degradation for instance family g4dn in ap-northeast1 at 1854322022. Quota available but spot capacity low. Logged CLOUD-9499.
yusuf: digging into scheduler: fractional-allocator module is active but there is a gating flag `bridge_accept` which seems to be default false in the global rollout config. The bridge-pool nodes are labeled but allocator rejects pods unless per-deployment annotation present.
pete: so tiny pods without `scheduler.alpha/bridge-allow=true` won't land, even though pool exists. That explains pending + idle bridge nodes. That's a bad default.
lina: quick mitigations I did: added `scheduler.alpha/bridge-allow=true` annotation to two high-volume tiny deployments as a canary. Patch command: `kubectl patch deploy mini-service -n prod -p '{"spec":{"template":{"metadata":{"annotations":{"scheduler.alpha/bridge-allow":"true"}}}}}'`
infra-bot: ALERT: [gpu-pending-pods] cluster-prod-ap-northeast1 threshold breached (count=72) at 1854322005
cloud-ops-bot: Provisioner attempted scale-up for bridge pool but spot bids failed twice at 1854322050. Fallback plan recommended: try a small on-demand burst or route low-priority jobs to ap-southeast1.
rachel: after annotation to a subset, pending dropped from 72 -> 20 within 9 minutes and bridge util rose from 22% -> 57%. Cost uptick noted (~7% for the bridge nodes) but acceptable to stabilize.
yusuf: immediate action items: 1) set `bridge_accept=true` default for the allocator while we complete per-deployment audit 2) add rollout gate so new pool features default to off only if pending_gpu_count < 15 for 20m 3) add per-region spot supply fallback to on-demand in provisioner.
pete: long-term: - make `bridge-allow` opt-out rather than opt-in - add scheduler unit test to ensure unlabeled tiny pods can use bridge-pool when pool capacity available - add canary for pool feature flags (5% of tiny deploys) - reduce lease TTL to 30s to accelerate rebalance.
lina: I've opened INFRA-2133 to track the bridge default bug + runbook: steps (1) annotate critical tiny deploys, (2) if spot failure persists, spin a small on-demand burst pool with `bridge-pool` tag, (3) revert the allocator default to accept. Assigned to @yusuf and @pete.
cloud-ops-bot: Created CLOUD-9499 (spot supply) and noted a workaround: try alternate instance family (g5s) or on-demand burst.
infra-bot: RESOLVED ALERT: pending_gpus returned to 18 at 1854322139
yusuf: follow-up: please add a CI preflight that runs a simulated packing check when adding new pool types/flags. Also add a quota/spot preflight for the region in the provisioner job.
pete: agreed. I'll PR the allocator default change and the canary rollout for bridge flags. Lina, paste INFRA-2133 link here when ready and let's schedule a short postmortem in the ops sync.
rachel: status at 1854322140: pending=12, bridge-pool util=54%. Leaving alerts on but removing paging. Thanks team.
